issues.legal_issue: A landholder may obtain an ejectment decree for a subletting that exceeds the permitted duration even when the tenant’s ability to recover possession from the subtenant remains unresolved.
material_facts: A tenant sublet the land to a subtenant under a year-to-year arrangement that continued for more than five years, contrary to the statutory limit on subletting.
The landholder sued the tenant and subtenant for ejectment based on the excessive subletting, and the record disclosed no defence to the suit.
The tenant’s application to evict the subtenant and the landholder’s application to execute the decree were still pending, leaving recovery of possession to be decided separately.
issues.conclusion: The landholder was entitled to the ejectment decree; whether possession could be recovered was a separate question for the pending proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 40 and 171 of the United Provinces Tenancy Act, 1939, a tenant’s subletting beyond the permitted period may support a landholder’s suit for ejectment against the tenant and the subtenant who entered possession. The continuation or termination of the subtenancy is distinct from recovery of possession: uncertainty about whether the tenant can evict the subtenant does not defeat the landholder’s entitlement to a decree. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.landholder_ejectment_suit: A landholder brought a suit seeking ejectment of a tenant and subtenant on the ground of unauthorized subletting.
predicates.subletting_exceeded_permitted_term: A tenant sublet land for longer than the duration permitted for that tenancy.
predicates.sublessee_entered_possession: A subtenant entered possession of the land under the subletting.
predicates.landholder_entitled_to_ejectment_decree: The landholder is entitled to an ejectment decree.

issues.definition: When a landholder seeks ejectment for a subletting beyond the permitted duration and the subtenant entered possession, the landholder is entitled to an ejectment decree.
